text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000133 bills 99215 well above what patient complexity predicts in every complexity band, including many low-complexity visits, but records came back for too few 99215 claims to confirm or rule out upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing pattern leans toward concern. The elevated 99215 share holds in every complexity band, not just among sicker patients, and a sizable share of 99215s fall on patients with 0–1 conditions. Examples include sampled claims C0067365 (J06.9, no chronic conditions) and C0067410 (R21 only), which are hard to square with high-complexity visits. The documentation does not confirm this. The few documented 99215s, including C0067548 and C0067720, support the billed level, and only one documented claim (C0067427, a 99214) fell below billed. But four documented 99215s is too thin to judge, and several supported notes lack recorded minutes. The small number of moderate-plus data-reviewed notes with no lab or test line on the claim is weak evidence of templated documentation, not proof. A reviewer should first request charts specifically for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed in the packet, checking whether MDM is genuinely high or the notes appear cloned. Next, they should check whether the heavy 99214 volume shows the same mismatch."}
